what_its_for: Mefenamic acid is a pain reliever used to treat mild to moderate pain. It is most commonly used to relieve painful menstrual periods (period cramps). It belongs to a group of medicines called NSAIDs (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs), which work by reducing substances in the body that cause pain and inflammation.
how_to_take: Take mefenamic acid by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Always take it with food, milk, or antacids to help protect your stomach and reduce the chance of an upset stomach. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking it. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. Take exactly as prescribed by your doctor and do not take more than directed.
dosing: The usual adult dose for pain is 500 mg (milligrams) to start, then 250 mg every 6 hours as needed. For menstrual cramps, the usual dose is 500 mg taken at the start of your period, then 250 mg every 6 hours for up to 3 days (or as directed by your doctor). Do not take more than 1,500 mg per day unless your doctor tells you otherwise. This medicine is generally not used for more than 7 days at a time.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you remember soon after, take it as soon as you can. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mefenamic acid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking mefenamic acid, as it increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take aspirin or other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen or naproxen) at the same time unless your doctor has told you to, as this can increase side effects. Avoid taking this medicine if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs, as a serious allergic reaction may occur. Be careful driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or drowsy. Avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: signs of stomach bleeding such as black, tarry, or bloody stools or vomiting blood; chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness, or slurred speech (signs of a heart attack or stroke); severe stomach pain or cramping; swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue (signs of an allergic reaction); difficulty breathing or skin rash; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or unusual tiredness (signs of liver problems); decreased urination or swelling in your legs or ankles (signs of kidney problems); or significant changes in your vision or hearing.
when_it_works: Mefenamic acid usually starts to relieve pain within 30 to 60 minutes after taking it. For best results with menstrual cramps, it works best when started at the first sign of your period or when cramps begin, rather than waiting until the pain becomes severe.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Use with extra caution. Older adults are at higher risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart-related side effects. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Do NOT use mefenamic acid during the last 3 months of pregnancy (third trimester), as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor before using it during any stage of pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Small amounts may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children under 14 years old has not been fully established. Do not give this medicine to a child without a doctor's guidance. Kidney or liver disease: Use with great caution. This medicine may worsen these conditions. Your doctor will decide if it is safe for you.
